title: Burst Computing: Quick, Sudden, Massively Parallel Processing on Serverless Resources
problem: Serverless platforms lack mechanisms to efficiently handle sudden bursts of massively parallel workloads, causing high latency and poor resource utilization for bursty parallel applications.
motivation: Many modern applications exhibit bursty parallel compute patterns that require rapid execution on shared cloud infrastructure without pre-provisioning.
method: The system coordinates parallel task execution across distributed serverless functions using optimized scheduling and resource allocation algorithms. It enables rapid provisioning and synchronization of parallel tasks through coordinated invocation patterns and dependency management.
key_novelty: Enabling efficient massively parallel computation on serverless platforms through burst-aware coordination and scheduling mechanisms.
contributions: System architecture for burst parallel computing on serverless infrastructure
Efficient scheduling algorithms for coordinating parallel tasks across serverless functions
Techniques for rapid provisioning and synchronization of distributed parallel workloads
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in the provided abstract.
